sentences.text: 1. Considered IA No.9291/2024, which is an application for dispensing with service of notice upon respondents 1 and 2 on the ground that the liability of the Insurance Company is not disputed.
2. For the reasons stated in the application the same is allowed and service of notice of this appeal upon respondents 1 and 2 is dispensed with at the risk of the appellant.
3. With the consent of learned counsel for the parties the matter is finally heard.

4. This appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 10.10.2023 passed in MACC No.348/2022 by the Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Dewas whereby a total sum of Rs.5,79,000/- has been awarded to him by way of compensation.
5. As per the appellant, on 26.11.2021 he was going along with his brother Ganesh from Dewas to Nevri in a Maruti Van.

When they reached NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6104 2 MA-181-2024 Budangaon, Nevri Road, respondent No.1 drove vehicle bearing registration No.MP-09-GF-7888 which was owned by respondent No.2 and was insured with respondent No.3 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against their vehicle.
In the accident appellant suffered grievous injuries.
He was taken to the hospital for treatment where he remained under treatment for a considerable period of time.

sentences.text: Thereafter the appellant filed an application under Section 166, 140 of the Act, 1988 before the Claims Tribunal for award of a total sum of Rs.48,50,000/- to him by way of compensation.
The non-applicants contested the application by filing their written statement to the same.
Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the appellant as aforesaid.
7. This appeal for enhancement of the amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellant on the ground that his income which has been taken at Rs.7,000/- per month is inordinately low.
He was a labourer and was having a puncture shop and was deriving sufficient income therefrom which hence ought to have been assessed accordingly.
It is further submitted that since in the accident the right hand of the appellant was amputated his permanent disability could not have been assessed at a mere 40%.
The doctor who had issued the Permanent Disability Certificate had opined the permanent disability to be 80% which hence should have been taken accordingly.
It is further submitted that the amount awarded for special diet, conveyance and attendant expenses is extremely low.
No amount has been awarded for loss of income and medical expenditure.
It is hence submitted that the amount awarded to the appellant be enhanced appropriately.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 Insurance Company NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:6104 3 MA-181-2024 has submitted that just and fair amount of compensation has been awarded to the appellant in which no interference is warranted in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
9. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
10. At the time of the accident the appellant was aged about 49 years and was hail and hearty.
He was having a puncture shop as has been stated by him in his evidence.
There was no reason to disbelieve the same.
The Claims Tribunal could not have expected the appellant to produce any documentary evidence in support of his contentions.
Considering the fact that the accident had taken place in the year 2021 the income of the appellant which has been assessed at Rs.7,000/- per month is extremely low.
The same in my opinion deserves to be taken at Rs.8,500/- per month.

11. The doctor who had issued the Permanent Disability Certificate of the appellant Dr. R.K.Sharma was examined as PW-3 before the Claims Tribunal who proved the Permanent Disability Certificate Ex.P/28 issued by him in which he stated the permanent disability of the appellant to be 80%.
The Claims Tribunal has however taken the same at only 40%.
In the accident right hand of the appellant which would have been his main hand for carrying on his job has been amputated rendering him virtually unfit for any further job.
His permanent disability hence deserves to be assessed at 75% for the entire body.
12. The amount which has been awarded under the heads of special diet, conveyance and attendant expenditure are quite low.
They deserve to be awarded at Rs.10,000/- each.
No amount has been awarded for loss of wages.
The appellant remained out of work for a period of three months hence the same is assessed at Rs.25,500/-.

The medical expenditure deserves to be awarded at Manoj vs Kanhaiyalal on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108313726/
2 Rs.10,000/-.

For NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6104 4 MA-181-2024 permanent disablement the appellant would be entitled for a sum of Rs.8,500/- + Rs.2,125/- (25% future prospects of rise in income) which would be Rs.10,625/- per month i.e. Rs.1,27,500/- annually.
Taking the permanent disability at 75% and applying the multiplier of 13 the amount which the appellant would be entitled for under permanent disablement would be Rs.12,43,125/-.

13. The appellant is hence entitled for a total amount of compensation in the sum of Rs.13,33,625/-
whereas the Claims Tribunal has erred in awarding him a sum of Rs.5,79,000/- only.

The appellant is hence held entitled for enhancement in the award of compensation in the sum of Rs.7,54,625/-
which shall be payable to him along with the same rate of interest as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of the claim application till the date of payment.
14. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.
